ReactNewContext > `reading context with.note: Each Provider level derives its value from the nearest outer Provider (value * 2) across shouldComponentUpdate bailouts. Stores are global; there's no nearest-Provider resolution to derive from.
Asserts that the same context reads the Provider's value inside it and the default value outside of it. A store has one value for every reader.
Asserts that the outer Provider value is restored after an inner Provider's subtree throws. Stores are global, so there's no shadowed value to restore.

ReactNewContext > Context.Provider > war.note: Warning about a Provider without a value prop. Stores have no Provider.

Warning about a Provider being rendered by two renderers at once, which context doesn't support. A store keeps a record per root, so concurrent renderers are supported, and there's no Provider to warn about ("works with multiple roots" in ReactUseStore-test covers the store side).

ReactNewContext > Context.Provider > doe.note: The negative of the multiple-renderers Provider warning. Nothing to warn about without a Provider.

ReactNewContext > Context.Provider > pro.note: Tests the Provider fiber's own bailout; the Child doesn't read context. Without a Provider there's nothing between App and its constant children.
Interaction between the Provider fiber's bailout and legacy context (childContextTypes). Stores have no Provider, and legacy context is out of scope.

ReactNewContext > Context.Consumer > war.note: Warning specific to rendering <Context.Consumer> without a function child.

ReactNewContext > readContext > can read.note: Uses the removed changedBits API (readContext with observed bits) and is gated FIXME in the original.

ReactNewContext > readContext > does not.note: The reader is a class component that calls readContext in render. Stores can't be read from class components. The same behavior is translated for function readers in the Context.Consumer and useContext versions of this case.

ReactNewContext > readContext > warns wh.note: Reads context inside a class's setState updater. Stores can't be read from class components, and the warning is context-specific.

ReactNewContext > should treat Context a.note: Asserts that Context.Provider === Context and that <Context value> provides.

ReactLazyContextPropagation > context ch.note: The reader is a PureComponent with static contextType, and the case is about that class re-rendering through its own bailout. Stores can't be read from class components; the memo HOC and useMemo versions are translated.

ReactHooks > hook ordering > `warns on u.note: useContext is one of the Hooks whose order is checked (useContextHelper in orderedHooks). use(store) takes no hook slot, so it can be called conditionally or in a different order without a warning ("can be read conditionally" in ReactUseStore-test pins that).

ReactHooks > hook ordering > `warns when.note: Same as the differently ordered hooks case: useContext appears in the hook order list, and use(store) takes no hook slot.

Heuristic false positive. These cases loop over hooksInList, which leaves out useContext. The checker flags them because secondHelper/hookNameB are bindings of the same names as in the orderedHooks loop, which does include useContext.

ReactHooks > hook ordering > warns on us.note: Heuristic false positive: it only uses useImperativeHandle and useMemo. The checker flags it through formatHookNamesToMatchErrorMessage, whose parameter names match the hookNameB binding of the orderedHooks loop.

ReactLazy > renders a lazy context provi.note: Lazy-loads the context object itself as a Provider type (Context.Provider === Context). A store isn't an element type, so there's nothing to lazy-load.
Same as "renders a lazy context provider".

ReactScope > ReactDOM > getChildContextV.note: Scope.getChildContextValues(Context) collects the values of the Providers in a scope. Stores have no Providers.

ReactUse > basic Context as node.note: Renders a Context object as a node (a Usable child). A store isn't a renderable node; rendering one throws "Objects are not valid as a React child" (checked by the server copies).

ReactUse > context as node, at the root.note: Same as "basic Context as node", at the root.

ReactUse > promises that resolves to a c.note: Same as "basic Context as node", through a promise.

readContext(Context) inside class compon.note: sharedContextTests runs once per way of reading context. This run reads context with readContext in a class's render. Stores can't be read from class components, so the copy only calls sharedContextTests for the four function readers.

readContext(Context) inside pure class c.note: Same as the class component run, with a PureComponent reader.
